$comment: Literal redactions for text that must never be written into this repository, and
that has no pattern to match it — research participant names above all.
placeholders.json holds regexes on purpose, so a rule never has to spell out the
text it removes. That works for anything with a shape. It does not work for the
name of a person in a client's interviews: there is no expression that matches
those and nothing else, and they are not knowable until the transcripts land.
So they live here, in a gitignored file, and the real one is GENERATED:
node buzz-agents/scripts/refresh-local-redactions.mjs \
--key ~/.buzz/.secrets/claire-<slug>-service-user.json \
--dataset research_<slug>
It reads participants.participant_name and conversations.document_name, so the
list derives from the data rather than from whoever last noticed a leak. Re-run it
after ingesting new transcripts: the guard only covers names it has seen.
This example file is committed; local-redactions.json is not. Copy it only if you
have a name to add by hand that the dataset does not carry.
find    the exact string. Matched on word boundaries where they apply, so a short
name does not rewrite the middle of an unrelated word. Under 3 characters
is refused as too collision-prone to be safe.
replace what appears instead.
label   what gets REPORTED when this matches. Never `find` — a leak warning that
prints the name it caught is the same exposure with extra steps.
